active_paradigms.idea: Iterative congestion-aware greedy with edge marginal-cost pricing (no LP/flow libs)
active_paradigms.description: Assign partitions one at a time globally (across all dsts, ordered by path-cost scarcity), recomputing Dijkstra with dynamically updated edge weights each time an edge gets used. Model the real evaluator cost: if cost is per-partition per-edge, penalize reuse; if shared edges amortize, discount reuse. Use G with weight = cost * (1 + alpha * current_edge_utilization/throughput) so later partitions naturally spread across parallel networks. This is a single repeated single-source Dijkstra loop, deterministic and fast.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: total transfer cost and load balance across parallel links
active_paradigms.cautions: Read evaluator.py first to determine whether repeated edge use costs linearly per partition or amortizes; set alpha accordingly. Avoid nx.min_cost_flow/linprog since they failed.

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing local search over per-partition route choices
active_paradigms.description: Start from the current best assignment (k-shortest paths per dst, one route per partition). Then run a lightweight simulated annealing / hill-climbing: propose swapping one (dst, partition) to another candidate route, compute the delta in the evaluator's exact cost model (including any throughput/penalty terms), accept per Metropolis criterion with a small temperature schedule (~a few thousand iterations, well within timeout). This directly optimizes the true objective rather than a linear proxy, which is likely why LP failed.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: exact evaluator score including any nonlinear congestion penalties
active_paradigms.cautions: Implement the evaluator's cost function faithfully as the objective; keep candidate sets small (k<=8) for speed; use a fixed random seed for determinism.
active_paradigms.approach_type: custom simulated annealing over scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment initialization

active_paradigms.idea: Amortized multicast tree via shared-segment packing with union of per-dst shortest paths
active_paradigms.description: Instead of per-partition routing, compute one shortest path per dst, then merge them into a shared-prefix tree: for each partition, reuse identical edge lists on shared segments so the evaluator (which may charge per unique edge or per transfer) sees minimal redundant transfers. For each dst, allow only a few partitions to deviate from the shared tree to parallel links when throughput limits bind. Key insight: encode paths so set_dst_partition_paths reuses the exact same edge objects for shared segments, minimizing counted transfers.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: redundant transfer reduction; number of distinct edges used
active_paradigms.cautions: Verify in evaluator.py whether cost scales with number of partitions traversing an edge or unique edges; nx.steiner_tree failed likely due to undirected/multi-commodity mismatch—use directed shortest-path merging instead, not Steiner.

tried_paradigms.idea: Build a directed Steiner tree so data is transferred once over shared links instead of independently per destination
tried_paradigms.description: The current algorithm computes an independent Dijkstra path from src to each dst and sends all num_partitions over each path, paying the full path cost once per destination. Instead, compute a Steiner tree connecting src to all dsts: use nx.steiner_tree on an undirected projection (or a directed variant by expanding the graph with reverse edges), then for each dst extract the unique src-to-dst path in the tree. Since the evaluator typically charges per edge used (or per unit of flow), shared prefix edges are paid once rather than once per destination, which is the dominant source of waste in the current solution. Assign all partitions to follow the tree path for each dst, appending edges via bc_topology.append_dst_partition_path. If the evaluator charges per-partition per-edge, then instead send only partition j over the tree path for dst j and rely on the tree structure to keep shared edges minimal, or split partitions across the tree paths evenly.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total data transfer cost by eliminating redundant transfers over shared path prefixes (multicast gain).
tried_paradigms.cautions: nx.steiner_tree works on undirected graphs; convert G to undirected with edge cost aggregation (min of the two directions), then map tree edges back to directed edges. Verify the evaluator's cost model (per-edge vs per-partition-per-edge) by inspecting evaluator.py to decide whether partitions should share the tree path or be split.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use k-shortest-path candidate sets plus a min-cost flow / linear assignment to spread partitions across parallel routes and balance load
tried_paradigms.description: First compute k alternative low-cost paths per destination using nx.shortest_simple_paths (generator, take first k). This exposes parallel network routes that plain Dijkstra ignores. Then formulate the partition-to-route assignment as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog: variables x[p][r] indicating partition p uses route r for each dst, with objective coefficients equal to route costs (possibly with congestion penalties if routes share edges), constraints that each partition is assigned exactly one route (sum_r x[p][r] = 1). If the evaluator penalizes throughput violations, add capacity constraints: for each edge, sum of flows over routes using it must be <= throughput. Solve the LP; fractional solutions can be rounded to the nearest integer assignment. This simultaneously exploits multi-network parallelism and load balancing, which the current single-path approach cannot.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Cost via route diversity and load balancing across parallel networks; avoidance of throughput-capacity penalties.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep k small (e.g., 5-10) so shortest_simple_paths generation doesn't time out. Build the LP constraint matrix carefully: capacity constraints only needed if evaluator enforces throughput. Round LP solutions deterministically (largest fractional remainder) to keep valid partition assignments.

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct min-cost multicast flow via nx.min_cost_flow on an expanded graph that encodes all partitions as separate commodities with shared-link discounts
tried_paradigms.description: Model the broadcast as a min-cost flow problem: create a super-sink, add an edge from each dst to the super-sink with demand = num_partitions (i.e., each destination needs all partitions), set node demand at src = num_partitions * len(dsts) if links are charged per unit, and give every edge capacity = its throughput and weight = its cost. Run nx.min_cost_flow (or nx.network_simplex) to get the globally optimal edge flows. Then decompose the resulting flow into per-destination paths by walking flow from src to each dst (flow decomposition), and register these paths per partition in BroadCastTopology. If the evaluator instead charges each edge only once regardless of volume, set all edge costs to 1 for used edges and demands to 1 per dst, which reduces to a Steiner-like solution but solved exactly as a flow problem on the directed graph (avoiding the undirected conversion issue).
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Globally minimal transfer cost under throughput capacity constraints, exact optimum rather than greedy per-destination shortest paths.
tried_paradigms.cautions: nx.min_cost_flow requires integer capacities/demands; throughput values are floats — scale and round them (e.g., multiply by 1000 and round). Flow decomposition must send each partition along a distinct path with positive residual flow. Handle unreachable dsts gracefully with try/except to avoid evaluation crashes.

tried_paradigms.idea: Shared-multicast-tree routing via Steiner tree approximation instead of per-destination shortest paths
tried_paradigms.description: Broadcast is fundamentally a multicast problem, so instead of routing each destination independently (which redundantly re-sends shared prefix edges once per dst per partition), build a single directed Steiner tree over the set {src} ∪ dsts using a cost-weighted version of G (with None costs replaced by a large finite penalty). NetworkX has no native directed Steiner tree, but you can implement the standard 2-approximation by computing pairwise shortest paths (nx.multi_source_shortest_path_length or all_pairs_dijkstra) and running a minimum spanning tree on the metric closure restricted to terminals (networkx.minimum_spanning_tree on the complete graph of terminals), then mapping back to original edges and pruning non-terminal leaves. Then assign the tree's edges to all num_partitions partitions (or split the tree's parallel arcs across partitions if edges have throughput limits). Because shared trunk edges are paid once logically per partition instead of once per destination, this eliminates the redundant-transfer component of the score that the current per-dst LP approach cannot avoid.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total data transfer cost by eliminating redundant transfers on shared edges; also reduces edge congestion/throughput violations since fewer edges carry flow
tried_paradigms.cautions: Steiner tree must be directed (use nx.DiGraph and check reachability); num_partitions must equal actual partitions P; handle None-cost edges with large finite weights so Dijkstra/Steiner pruning works.

tried_paradigms.idea: Joint min-cost flow with capacity constraints using networkx max_flow_min_cost per partition, not per-destination
tried_paradigms.description: The current LP ignores throughput/capacity constraints entirely (it only penalizes congestion softly), which likely causes throughput violations in the evaluator. Formulate the whole problem as a min-cost multi-commodity flow: create a super-sink node T; for each destination dst add edges dst→T with demand num_partitions (one unit per partition); src has supply num_partitions*len(dsts). Set each edge capacity from G's 'throughput' attribute and cost from 'cost'. Solve with a min-cost-flow LP: variables f[e] per edge per commodity, minimize sum(cost[e]*f[e]) subject to flow conservation per node per commodity and sum over commodities of f[e] <= throughput[e]. Build this as a single scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) call over all variables jointly. Recover per-dst per-partition paths by flow decomposition of each commodity's flow into num_partitions unit paths (standard successive-shortest-path decomposition along positive-flow edges). This directly encodes the evaluator's real constraints and objective rather than approximating them.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Throughput violation penalties (edges where flow >= throughput) while keeping transfer cost low; jointly optimizes cost and feasibility rather than trading them via a soft congestion penalty
tried_paradigms.cautions: The min-cost flow LP relaxes the integer path requirement; a partition's flow may split across edges — handle by rounding fractional flows or by adding per-partition unit-commodity structure; None throughput values must be imputed (e.g., 0 or a small default); respect the evaluator's flow < throughput (strict) constraint when setting capacities.

tried_paradigms.idea: Global route assignment across all destinations and partitions with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment
tried_paradigms.description: The current algorithm processes destinations greedily/one at a time so early destinations grab the cheapest paths and later ones are pushed onto expensive or congested routes. Instead, generate K candidate paths per destination (nx.shortest_simple_paths with cost weight, but also generate a second set using a composite weight cost*(1+alpha*expected_load) for diversity), then build a global assignment problem: for each (dst, partition) pair, choose one candidate route such that no edge is overloaded (total assigned flow on an edge < its throughput) and total cost is minimized. This is an integer program; approximate it by iterating scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment: first assign all (dst,partition) units to their cheapest routes, then repeatedly detect overloaded edges, and for each overloaded edge use linear_sum_assignment on the set of units using it versus their next-best alternative routes (cost matrix = incremental route cost), swapping to resolve violations. This is a single library-driven repair loop, not multi-stage optimization of a tuned model.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Overall scalar score by balancing load globally across all dsts simultaneously; removes the ordering bias of sequential per-dst processing and reduces throughput violations
tried_paradigms.cautions: Must synthesize enough diverse route candidates per dst (increase K to ~12-20 and include paths that are cheap under throughput congestion, not just pure cost); blocked edges with infinite cost must never be assigned (add guard rows/columns); verify each produced path is simple and starts at src ends at dst.
